name: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak
nameAr: عبد الله بن المبارك بن واضح الحنظلي التميمي مولاهم المروزي

nisbas.en: al-Hanzali (as a client of Banu Hanzala)

diedNote: 181 AH aged 63, at Hit on the Euphrates on his way back from a campaign (Taqrib; Shamela record); also said 182

taqrib.ar: ثقة ثبت فقيه عالم جواد مجاهد، جمعت فيه خصال الخير
taqrib.en: Reliable and firm, a jurist and scholar, generous, a fighter in God's cause; every good quality was gathered in him.

role: Imam of Khurasan; hadith master, jurist, ascetic and author

teachers.name: Sufyan al-Thawri
teachers.source: Shamela narrator record 2472 names Ibn al-Mubarak among Sufyan's companions; Tahdhib al-Kamal 16/5 (Ibn Mahdi's comparison of the two)

teachers.name: Hammad ibn Zayd
teachers.source: reciprocal of the entry in hammad-ibn-zayd's record (Tahdhib al-Tahdhib)

teachers.name: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid
teachers.source: reciprocal of the entry in ismail-ibn-abi-khalid's record (Tahdhib al-Tahdhib)

verdicts.ar: عبد الله بن المبارك ثقة إمام

verdicts.en: Ibn al-Mubarak is the imam of the Muslims.

verdicts.ar: ما رأت عيناي مثل أربعة: ما رأيت أحفظ للحديث من الثوري، ولا أشد تقشفا من شعبة، ولا أعقل من مالك بن أنس، ولا أنصح للأمة من عبد الله بن المبارك
verdicts.en: My eyes have not seen the like of four men: none with a better memory for hadith than al-Thawri, none more austere than Shu'ba, none wiser than Malik ibn Anas, and none more sincerely devoted to the community than Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak.

verdicts.ar: كان فيه خصال لم تجتمع في أحد من أهل العلم في زمانه في الأرض كلها
verdicts.en: He had qualities that were not combined in any other scholar of his age anywhere on earth.

verdicts.ar: هو إمام عصره في الآفاق، وأولاهم بذلك علما وزهدا وشجاعة وسخاء
verdicts.en: He is the imam of his age throughout the lands, and the most deserving of that title in learning, asceticism, courage and generosity.

dhahabi.source: al-Kashif, as quoted on the Shamela narrator record

bio: The great scholar of Marw, a merchant who spent his wealth on students and campaigns, and the author of some of the earliest books of hadith and asceticism. He travelled widely and heard from Yunus ibn Yazid and Ma'mar, the two main carriers of al-Zuhri's hadith, which is why he can join their reports in a single chain. He died at Hit in 181 AH returning from the frontier. Abdan and Bishr ibn Muhammad, al-Bukhari's two teachers in this hadith, were both his students in Marw.

provenance.ref: Shamela narrator record 3875, drawing on Tahdhib al-Kamal 16/5 and Tahdhib al-Tahdhib 2/415
